back: A pre-contract information problem: lenders cannot distinguish high-risk from low-risk borrowers, so raising rates worsens the borrower pool.
A post-contract information problem: once insured or funded, an agent takes more risk because they do not bear the full downside.
In a panic, a central bank should lend freely, at a penalty rate, against good collateral. Distinguishes liquidity support from solvency bailout.
CET1: 4.5% of RWA. Tier 1: 6%. Total capital: 8%. Capital conservation buffer: +2.5% CET1. G-SIB surcharge: up to +3.5%.
Equity tranche (first loss) → Mezzanine → Senior → Super-senior (last loss). Higher seniority = lower yield = higher rating.
Good: only early consumers withdraw; bank solvent. Bad: all depositors run (self-fulfilling panic); bank insolvent from forced liquidation.
Banks' expected loan return is non-monotonic in r. At r*, it peaks. Beyond r*, raising rates worsens pool quality → banks ration credit at r* rather than raise rates.
F/S = (1+r_d)/(1+r_f). Forward premium = interest differential. Arbitrage enforces CIP. Deviations = cross-currency basis; signal funding stress.
1. Sale of business. 2. Bridge institution. 3. Asset separation (bad bank). 4. Bail-in. Applied by resolution authority when PONV is met.
Trigger for resolution under BRRD: bank is failing or likely to fail AND no private solution available AND resolution is in public interest.
Insurance value = put option on bank assets with strike = face value of deposits. Premium rises with leverage (D/A) and asset volatility (σ).
Norway: full state ownership of three largest banks; shareholders wiped out. Sweden: blanket guarantee on all bank liabilities + bad banks (Securum). Both resolved without depositor losses.
Short-term paper (≤270 days) issued by conduits/SIVs to fund longer ABS. When markets froze Aug 2007, SIVs could not roll; sponsors forced to absorb back onto balance sheet.
Price fall → higher margins → forced selling → further price fall → wider spreads. Funding and market liquidity spiral together; amplified by VaR constraints.
